title: Monday · learning, creating and sharing
arrival: Answer attendance, then hand in forms and get your work ready.
note: Flexible subject blocks with time to finish current work and improve existing SpacesEDU postings. Continue from the actual class stopping points. Prioritise first-term work already assigned; new learning can become second-term evidence later, without a new posting deadline today. Keep snack, recess, lunch, cleanup and dismissal routines.

blocks.title: Welcome and attendance
studentSteps: Answer attendance, then hand in forms.
Check today’s plan and choose your first useful task.

blocks.title: Mathematics
blocks.firstAction: Open your current math work and find your next step.
studentSteps: Finish or correct your current work.
Show your steps and explain one strategy.
If ready, model the same amount as a mixed number and an improper fraction.
blocks.notes: Prioritise current math evidence and feedback. If ready, use equal-sized wholes to show 7/4 = 1 3/4. Do not assume previous work is finished or require a new submission.

blocks.title: Language Arts · Nevermoor and writing
blocks.firstAction: Find where we stopped in Nevermoor.
studentSteps: Listen or read from our bookmark.
Use a detail from the story to explain a character’s choice or make a prediction.
Continue your current reading or writing response.
blocks.notes: Use the actual book/audio bookmark, not a guessed chapter. Allow time for current Language Arts work and its existing SpacesEDU evidence.

blocks.title: Snack
blocks.firstAction: Have your snack and tidy your space.

blocks.title: Social Studies · country inquiry
blocks.firstAction: Open your current inquiry notes or choose a question with your teacher.
studentSteps: Choose one question about people’s lives, rights or access.
Find a useful source detail and record where it came from.
Compare what you know with what you still need to find out.
blocks.notes: Continue or introduce the existing two-country inquiry according to readiness. Use one manageable question. Avoid ranking whole countries from one example. Fieldnotes does not autosave: download or print notes before closing. This is preparation for later second-term evidence, not a new deadline.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.firstAction: Follow our outside-play and lunch routine.

blocks.title: Quiet reset
blocks.firstAction: Choose quiet reading, drawing or another calm activity.

blocks.title: ADST · Bloxels design
blocks.firstAction: Open your existing Bloxels project or planning page.
studentSteps: Choose one part of your game or story to improve.
Build or revise it, then test whether it works as intended.
Record one change you made and why.
blocks.notes: Continue the existing project rather than inventing a new assignment. Use planning on paper where helpful; connect changes to the intended player experience.

blocks.title: SpacesEDU · finish and share learning
blocks.firstAction: Open the unfinished posting your teacher has asked you to work on.
studentSteps: Finish the work and choose clear evidence.
Explain what you learned using a specific example.
Check the existing instructions and feedback.
Save or submit as your teacher directs.
blocks.notes: Prioritise the current first-term postings. Additional completion time can be used within subject blocks. Do not create new assignments or infer teacher assessment/publication.

blocks.title: Tidy, movement and community
blocks.firstAction: Save your work, put materials away and complete your classroom job.
studentSteps: Save your progress and return materials.
Join a short movement break when directed.
Share a useful learning moment and record confirmed reminders.

blocks.title: Pack up and dismissal
blocks.firstAction: Check your belongings and get ready for a calm departure.

backups: Adjust subject-block lengths to the work students need to complete; retain the fixed breaks and dismissal.
Use notebooks, paper plans and teacher-guided discussion when useful.
Keep existing deadlines and allow unfinished work to continue in school; no new posting deadline is added.
